title: Executive Summary
headline: The rolling horizon runs 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18: 25 games (2026-11-16=8, 2026-11-17=5, 2026-11-18=12), each with an originated line, a paper-pick row and an injury read-out, published pre-tip with pre-registration frozen at 2026-11-16T00:16Z and hash-chained into a 5-entry ledger (head 18a25667…). The 2026-11-14 slate is settled from official finals: singles 1W-2L-1P-1NB (-1.2u), parlays 0-3 (-3.3u), SGP 1-1 (+2.26u), total -2.24u at the -110 paper convention. On 2026-11-16 this window's schedule was read directly from nba.com for the first time in the project's history and matched the stored capture exactly on every game, tip time and venue.
lead: Ten strategies were written, seven validation gates were defined, and all ten were run against a strictly out-of-sample window: all 60 completed games from 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-13, every one predicted using team ratings computed only from 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05. No game in the test window contributes to the ratings that predict it. The three official team-stat pages (traditional, opponent, advanced) were re-read on 2026-11-15 and the model inputs re-cut from them. The system originates a line for every game in the current rolling window — 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18, 25 games (2026-11-16=8, 2026-11-17=5, 2026-11-18=12) — plus the newest official injury report. Pre-registration for this window was frozen at 2026-11-16T00:16Z, 23.8 hours before the first tip (2026-11-16, ORL@BOS, 7:00 PM ET = 2026-11-17T00:00Z), and the current roll publishes 25 singles (24 model picks), 9 parlays and 6 SGP candidates. The 2026-11-14 slate is closed out and stamped. The 2026-11-15 slate is NOT settled: at 21:29 ET on 11/15 six of its nine games were final and three were still in progress, and the brief's rule is to settle only after final scores are verified. A second session re-read the same official sources independently at 2026-11-16T02:12-02:17Z and its measurements are carried here too: home-court advantage pinned to the measured official home-win rate of 0.5285, worth 1.23 points, rather than fitted freely; 14 of the 25 picks clear every model gate and none is publishable outright, because no official injury edition covers 11/17 or 11/18 yet and five 11/16 teams still print NOT YET SUBMITTED.

verdict.one_line: The model beats the naive reference on margin accuracy (MAE 12.98 against 13.62) and loses to it on totals (14.83 against 14.72) and on picking winners (42-18 against 40-20). S1 (side edge) is now 23-9, worth +11.91 model units, and for the first time its record is outside what luck alone produces (exact binomial p = 0.020, Wilson lower bound 0.546 against the 0.524 break-even) - but it fails the calibration gate (hit rate 0.719 against a mean predicted 0.627) and the stability gate (the bootstrap interval on the model's margin MAE still overlaps the reference), and the availability gate cannot run at all. Under the tier ceilings it stays a quarter-unit strategy. The 34 games of the 15-18 Nov roll are published as lines and paper picks, not as recommendations.
verdict.why: Sixty games with a 17.4-point residual standard deviation have finally made one record statistically distinguishable from a coin flip - and that is exactly when the other gates matter most. A hit rate the model itself did not predict is a calibration failure, not a windfall; an improvement whose interval overlaps the reference is not stable; and a gate that cannot run is not passed. Selective skill means paying for the part that survives every gate and nothing else.

findings.title: The model wins on the margin and loses on totals and winners
findings.detail: Margin: MAE 12.98 against 13.62 for the naive reference, RMSE 17.12 against 17.88 - the model is better on both. Totals: MAE 14.83 against 14.72, RMSE 19.35 against 19.10 - the reference is better on both. Straight up the reference went 42-18 and the model 40-20, and the reference has the better Brier score (0.2001 against 0.2020) and the better log loss (0.5827 against 0.5873).
findings.reading: The refinements buy a real but tiny margin improvement and nothing else. The probability calibration is the weakest part of the model, and it is where the remaining work should go.

findings.title: Growing the window keeps changing what can be claimed - which is the point of the sample gate
findings.detail: On the 28-game window the model beat the reference on totals (MAE 14.50 against 14.75). On 51 games it did not (14.86 against 14.75) - the sign flipped. On the 60-game window the sign holds (14.83 against 14.72) and the gap narrowed, but the conclusion stands. Each addition of data has moved at least one claim.
findings.reading: Any single-window result at this sample size should be treated as a hypothesis, not a finding.

findings.title: S1 has cleared the luck gate at 23-9 - and failed two others, which is the honest headline
findings.detail: S1 (side edge vs the reference spread) produced 32 graded plays at 23-9, worth +11.91 model units and a 37.2% return at -110. Its exact binomial p-value against a coin flip is 0.020 and the Wilson 95% interval on its hit rate is 0.546 to 0.844 - the lower bound is now above the 0.5238 break-even, so G4 (skill, not luck) passes for the first time. But its hit rate of 0.719 against a mean predicted probability of 0.627 fails the calibration gate (gap 0.091 against a 0.08 tolerance), and the stability gate fails because the bootstrap interval on the model's margin MAE (10.2 to 15.94) still contains the reference MAE (13.62). The availability gate cannot run at all for the graded window.
findings.reading: This is what selectively skill-based looks like: one gate says this is probably not luck, two gates say the model does not understand why, and the funding tier stays at quarter unit until every gate that can be run has been run and passed.

findings.title: Home court looks normal; the back-to-back penalty is large but uncertain
findings.detail: Home-court advantage estimates at +3.51 points with a standard error of 2.28 (t = 1.54) across 60 games, squarely in the historical NBA range. The back-to-back penalty estimates at -6.26 points with a standard error of 4.86 (t = -1.29); because |t| >= 1 the model applies the full 6.26, but the standard error is most of the estimate.
findings.reading: Both are published with their standard errors and both are fitted on the test window, which is disclosed on every row they touch.

findings.title: Shrinkage was derived rather than guessed, and the curve is flat where it matters
findings.detail: The empirical-Bayes calculation gives k = 2.9, weighting each team's observed net rating at 0.739. The fixed-k sweep shows margin MAE moving from 13.62 at k = 0 to 12.91 at k = 4, then degrading to 13.36 by k = 20. Heavy shrinkage is clearly wrong; the choice between light and none barely matters.
findings.reading: The constant is defensible, its sensitivity is published, and it is not a source of hidden risk.

findings.title: Availability impact is a measured floor, not an estimate
findings.detail: Minutes are only known for the 50 players in the captured official table. Players outside it contribute 0.00 to the impact, so teams missing rotation players who are not top-50 scorers show a smaller number than the truth - sometimes zero. The minutes-coverage column sits next to every figure so a 0.00 is never read as 'healthy'.
findings.reading: Correct but incomplete - the Injuries page says so on every row rather than hiding it.

findings.title: Correlation is measured where it can be and flagged where it cannot
findings.detail: Thirteen team-statistic pairs were measured directly on all 30 teams from the official advanced table. Net rating explains 87% of the variation in win percentage; pace is nearly unrelated to net rating (r = -0.34, p = 0.063) and assist percentage is unrelated to offensive efficiency (r = 0.02, p = 0.92). The parlay and same-game-parlay correlations that drive pricing are model-derived and labelled as such.
findings.reading: The distinction matters most for parlays, because pricing correlated legs as independent is the classic way to overpay.

findings.title: The word 'edge' on this site does not mean edge against a sportsbook
findings.detail: No sportsbook price is published by an NBA-operated source, so no official link can be attached to one. The site bets the originated line against a deliberately naive reference model built from the same official ratings. Until real prices are logged, 'units won' means model-vs-naive-model units.
findings.reading: This is the single most important caveat for anyone reading the leaderboard.

findings.title: The 2026-11-13 slate is settled, and it did not go well - which is the system working
findings.detail: Every published paper pick on the 2026-11-13 slate was settled against the official finals captured on 2026-11-14. The seven gated singles went 3-4 (-1.40 units at -110) and all three two-leg parlays lost. The picks were pre-registered: the model blocks in the live file are identical to the copy frozen at 2026-11-13T22:45Z, before tip. The originated margin line was off by 12.39 points on average across the nine games - consistent with the 12.98 MAE on the wider window, and a useful reminder that a night like this is normal at this sample size.
findings.reading: Two gaps closed the same morning: the finals now exist (F13 resolved) and the 18 stale team records were refreshed from the official cards (F14 resolved). Two remain open and are published as such: at the newest injury edition five of the ten teams playing on 11/14 have still not filed, and no edition lists any player for the 11/16 and 11/17 games.

findings.title: The 60-game extension is real, but it cannot be reproduced from this repository alone
findings.detail: The 2026-11-13 finals are captured, transcribed three independent times that all agree 9/9, and used to settle every published 11/13 pick (seven singles 3-4 at -1.40 units, three two-leg parlays 0-3). That part is solid and was recomputed in a separate integration session with the same answer. What is NOT reproducible here is the extended metric: the 51->60 window and the 12.98 vs 13.62 margin MAE depend on a team-ratings refresh, and https://www.nba.com/stats/teams/advanced?Season=2026-27&SeasonType=Regular+Season returns no data table to this environment (flag F24, re-tested 2026-11-14). The committed ratings snapshot is still the one captured at 2026-11-14T00:38Z, whose season-to-date window predates the 11/13 games.
findings.reading: A reader can check every score and every settlement row against NBA.com, and should. The 60-game error metric they cannot check, because the inputs that would produce it are not retrievable. Treat the settlement as verified and the extended error metric as reported-but-not-reproducible until the ratings capture is automated.

findings.title: The game-day edition arrived, and it moved the model far less than it should have
findings.detail: New Orleans, Cleveland, Chicago and Miami filed between the 04:15 AM ET edition the horizon was cut from and the 01:30 PM ET game-day edition, adding 24 player rows and changing four statuses; Memphis was still inside its filing window. Re-run through the engine's own availability adjustment, that edition moves 3 of the 5 games tipping tonight (DAL@CLE -1.8 to -2.5; DET@MIA -12.2 to -12.4; CHI@MIN 30.6 to 33.2) and leaves DEN@NOP, BKN@MEM unchanged. No favourite flips and no published pick changes side.
findings.reading: Two readings are available and the site publishes both. The charitable one: intra-day report churn is usually noise, and a model that lurched on every status label would be worse. The uncomfortable one: the reason it cannot move New Orleans is that the Pelicans' five listed names are not in the minutes table, so the model is not judging them, it is blind to them. That is F47, and it is the highest-value item in the register.

findings.title: The published site is stale by one build — and the cause is a queue, not a bug
findings.detail: The GitHub Pages API reports status 'errored' for the current head, and the live URL was still serving the last successful build (afc79f2, 2026-11-16T00:51:58Z), which carries the previous 15–18 Nov horizon. Measured at 02:1x UTC: 20 probe runs were in_progress and 24 were queued — 44 concurrent runs of a workflow that takes ~1 hour each, because it triggered on every push to every arena/** branch. GitHub runs a bounded number of jobs per account and queues the rest FIFO, so the production Pages run sat pending for 43m55s. The push trigger has been removed, the concurrency group is now global, and the job has a 20-minute ceiling.
findings.reading: Nothing in the build was broken — check_site, verify_integration, check_links, check_rendered and verify_all all pass on the current head. The site was starved. This is the same class of defect SG23 fixed for pages.yml in §33; it had simply never been applied to the probe workflow.

findings.title: nba.com is reachable from this environment — flag F7 is finally answerable with data
findings.detail: Every prior session recorded that its sandbox could not reach nba.com, so the refresh path had never been executed (flag F7). This session read the official pages directly. Result for the 25-game window: every date, matchup, game ID and tip time is an EXACT MATCH against the stored capture. 15 record cells differ, and every one is explained — the stored capture was taken at 18:47 ET before tip, this read at 21:29 ET, after six 11/15 games had gone final. Standings: 30 teams read live; 10 cells differ and those 10 are exactly the participants in the five games that finished after the stored capture. No unexplained cell.
findings.reading: The schedule layer is verified, not assumed. The one honest gap: SAC's standings row fell across a fetch chunk boundary, so its W-L (1-11) comes from the official games page and the remaining cells are left null rather than inferred.

findings.title: Denver filed after the lines were cut — the exact gap §42 flagged
findings.detail: Diffing the two newest official injury editions (11/15 06:15 PM → 09:00 PM) for the 11/16 games: zero player-level status changes, one team submission change. Denver had submitted nothing at 06:15 PM and filed four players Out at 09:00 PM (Holmes II, Nembhard, Strawther, Whitmore) for PHX@DEN. Five teams had still not submitted at 09:00 PM: WAS, BOS, HOU, PHI and PHX.
findings.reading: The lines for 2026-11-16 were cut from the 06:15 PM edition, so PHX@DEN is priced without Denver's four Out players. §42 identified precisely this class of gap. The lines were NOT re-priced here: a line re-priced after publication cannot be graded. The newer edition is published alongside so a reader can see the difference.

findings.title: A defect in the repository's own injury encoding, found by the diff and now detectable
findings.detail: data/official/injury_2026-11-15_0615PM.json encodes the Boston Celtics NOT-YET-SUBMITTED marker as status='Out', player='Penda, Noah'. 'Penda, Noah' is inherited from the preceding Orlando row — the league prints no player on a NOT YET SUBMITTED row. Any consumer reading the status column counts a player who was never named as ruled out for a team that had filed nothing. The diff now detects this encoding in both the status and the reason field rather than assuming it away.
findings.reading: Small, but it is the kind of defect that silently inflates an availability adjustment. Three further defects on the Injuries banner itself were fixed in the same pass: a blank revision stamp, an empty href="", and a raw Python dict rendered into the page with two wrong counts.

findings.title: The 2026-11-15 slate cannot be settled yet, and the site says so
findings.detail: At 21:29 ET on 11/15 six of the nine games were final (PHI 131-124 IND, LAL 131-123 PHX, LAC 113-105 CHA, SAS 110-102 UTA, BOS 131-94 DAL, NYK 112-108 TOR in OT) and three were in progress (HOU@WAS Q4 5:24, ATL@MIL Q3 10:42, OKC@SAC Q1 7:59). The brief's rule is that a row is FINAL only when the official page prints Final and the quarter linescores sum to it.
findings.reading: Settling a slate while games are live would put unverified scores into the ledger. The 11/15 slate stays open and will settle at game-day end from official finals.

findings.title: Provenance, not the availability percentage, is the honest output of the injury layer
findings.detail: Only 4 of the 25 picks have a measured rotation availability for the pick team. The rest are blank for a stated reason: no official edition covers the game date (11/17 and 11/18), the team's entry prints NOT YET SUBMITTED (WAS, BOS, HOU, PHI, PHX on 11/16), or per-player minutes were never captured for that team. Before this pass the column silently read 100% for those cases and was labelled MEASURED, which was wrong - an empty injury list is not evidence that nobody is injured.
findings.reading: A blank cell with a reason is more decision-useful than a confident 100%. The fix is to make the refresh re-read the injury index so the column fills in game date by game date (SG36), and to capture minutes for all thirty teams so redistribution is computable everywhere (SG32).

what_is_live_now: Originated spreads, totals, moneylines and fair prices for all 25 games across 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18 (2026-11-16=8, 2026-11-17=5, 2026-11-18=12), generated 2026-11-15T23:55Z by scripts/originate_horizon.py from the newest official schedule capture.

25 pick rows on the rolling slate (24 priced singles and 1 gate pass-through no-bet), 9 two-leg parlays and 6 SGP candidates, each tagged with the gate decision — all MODEL OUTPUT, unvalidated, zero stake.

Pre-registration frozen at 2026-11-16T00:16Z for 25 games, hash-chained into data/ledger/ledger.json (5 entries, head 18a25667d251d2596b157dba6e06516514eb57e112e29d846902eba5085395c0), verified by scripts/verify_ledger.py.

The settlement of every published paper pick on the 2026-11-14 slate against official finals (singles 1-2-1 with 1 no-bet at -1.2u, parlays 0-3 at -3.3u, SGP 1-1 at +2.26u, total -2.24u), with the pre-registration check confirming the model blocks are byte-identical to the pre-tip anchor commit ef2e723.
The out-of-sample backtest on 60 games (2026-11-06 to 2026-11-13): margin MAE 12.98 against 13.62 for the naive reference, totals MAE 14.83 against 14.72, straight-up 40-20 against 42-18.

A live official re-verification of the whole 25-game window, read directly from nba.com on 2026-11-16 (see verify/2026-11-16-c348e6c7/): schedule, standings and the newest injury edition, compared cell by cell against the stored captures.
Two estimators per game with their disagreement published as the headline confidence signal (max 1.37 pp, mean 0.45 pp, gate 4.0 pp) and the blend underneath.
Home-court advantage pinned to the measured official home-win rate: 0.5285 from the standings HOME/ROAD columns (102 of 193), cross-checked at 0.5155 from the final-score corpus, worth 1.23 points.
A rotation-availability column per pick that states its own provenance - measured, not yet published, not yet submitted, or not captured - and is blank whenever it is not measured.
Measured parlay correlations (home/away points 0.0823, margin/total -0.0115, home points/total 0.732) with the rho-priced figure printed beside the naive product.
A per-game results feed for 2026-11-15: six finals stored, three games still in progress and marked not settleable, with quarter scores left null rather than reconstructed.

The official injury edition 11/15 09:00 PM with its revision and retrieval stamps, and its diff against the 06:15 PM edition: two real status changes (Ajay Mitchell Questionable to Available, Precious Achiuwa Questionable to Out).
Rest, back-to-back, 3-in-4 and travel distance for every team in the window, computed from the official schedule and a sourced arena-coordinate table.
A luck z-score per team, with the rule that a pick leaning on a team outside the +/-1.5 band is not published (it currently removes GSW twice and SAS once).
Six new flags (F101-F106), five new suggestions (SG32-SG36) and five new open questions (Q26-Q30), all published on the site with their official source links.

recommended_next_actions.action: Switch GitHub Pages to publish from GitHub Actions (repository admin, one setting)
recommended_next_actions.why: Pages is currently build_type=legacy (branch main, path /), so actions/deploy-pages in pages.yml can never publish and the site depends on GitHub's branch build, which is what left it serving a stale build. Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions. This session's token returns HTTP 403 on the Pages API, so it cannot be done from here.

recommended_next_actions.action: Settle the 2026-11-15 slate from official finals once its last game goes final
recommended_next_actions.why: Six of nine were final at 21:29 ET and three were live. The settlement rule requires the official page to print Final with quarter linescores summing to it; settling early would put unverified scores in the ledger.

recommended_next_actions.action: Complete the minutes input per club so the availability layer sees a rotation, not a top-50 slice
recommended_next_actions.why: It is what turns the 0.00 impact columns into numbers and unblocks Q3, Q12 and Q20. Until then the availability gate cannot run at all, which is one of the two gates keeping S1 at a quarter unit.

recommended_next_actions.action: Fix the calibration layer before adding strategies
recommended_next_actions.why: S1's hit rate is 0.719 against a mean predicted 0.627 — a gap of 0.091 against a 0.08 tolerance. A model that wins more often than it predicted is not better calibrated, and every downstream price inherits that error.

recommended_next_actions.action: Log real closing prices from any source and re-open gates G4, G5 and G-PROP
recommended_next_actions.why: No NBA-operated source publishes a price, so 'edge' on this site means model-versus-naive-reference. Without logged prices nothing here can be called profitable — only internally consistent.

recommended_next_actions.action: DONE 2026-11-14T19:20Z: capture the day-of-game injury updates and re-price against them. The published lines were deliberately not rewritten.
recommended_next_actions.why: Executed by session arena/95c1cb23-nba1. The two editions, the diff, the impact re-computation and the row-level verification are in data/derived/gameday_read.json, one source URL per row. The residual finding is F47: the availability layer cannot see most of what was filed.

recommended_next_actions.action: Capture the 11/16, 11/17 and 11/18 injury-report editions as they are published
recommended_next_actions.why: The 11/15/26 06:15 AM ET edition is captured (101 rows; its 11/16 team blocks print NOT YET SUBMITTED, exactly as the reporting deadlines predict). Each remaining edition should be stored with its revision and retrieval time and diffed against the previous one, as was done for 11/15 (F74).

recommended_next_actions.action: Backfill results for 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05 and re-cut the split
recommended_next_actions.why: Every game from 2026-11-06 onward is already in the test window, so this is now the only way to grow the sample. It would let the ratings window move earlier and the test window roughly double again.

recommended_next_actions.action: Re-read the injury index inside the scheduled refresh so availability fills in per game date.
recommended_next_actions.why: No official edition covers 11/17 or 11/18 yet and five 11/16 teams print NOT YET SUBMITTED (F105). Availability is the fastest-moving input and is currently only as fresh as the last session that looked.

bottom_line: The 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18 window (25 games) is published pre-tip, pre-registered and hash-chained, and its schedule was verified line by line against nba.com. Nothing on this site is a recommendation: no strategy has passed every validation gate, the market-anchored prior and prop pricing gates remain blocked pending an odds feed, and the -2.24u on the 11/14 slate is a paper record at the repo's -110 convention. Two things need the owner's attention: GitHub Pages is configured to publish from a branch rather than from GitHub Actions, so the actions/deploy-pages job in pages.yml cannot publish here (one admin setting fixes it, and this session's token does not have it); and the 11/15 slate settles only after its last game goes final. Open items for a reviewer: the SGP void convention (Q22), the SGP paper price (Q23), the refresh-cadence choice (SG30), the OT-column reconciliation (SG31), and the inherited-name rows in the stored injury editions.
